description: The placement that actually DISCRIMINATES the procedure boundary for this row, and the one every other `repcount` fixture in the corpus misses. A `define` written at the top level is not on a turn of anything to begin with, so a checker that let a procedure body inherit its surrounding answer still gets `scoping/repcount-does-not-cross-the-procedure-boundary` right. A `define` nested in a `repeat` body is legal (it is registered globally in phase 1, spec/execution-model.md's Reader pipeline) and is where the two implementations part: "dynamic loop state does not cross the procedure boundary any more than a variable does" (spec/execution-model.md:673-678), so `show_turn`'s body has no enclosing `repeat` of its own even though a `repeat` is running AND lexically encloses its text. The second `define` pins the same seal for a parameter default, which is evaluated per call inside the frame rather than on the caller's turn. Measured: `execute()` agrees, raising at line 3 — and stopping there, which is why the second read needs the semantic stage to be seen at all. Measured too: this is the ONLY fixture in the corpus that goes red when the seal is removed (1048 passed, 1 failed).
